unbaked.why: The door-gradient lane (the door bands, the oracle's asking and seed door), the family-turn-settle lane (the clock sweeper: a held family turn waits on its settle and answers owed, never on a timer), the in-flight backstop lane (a framed root edited during a held placement places again on settle), and the fold (the filter module lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/filters/meme-fold with the meme-fold and spirit-fold operators, the macro lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/macros/spirit-unfold and the code-meme lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/heleuma/meme-fold), the projection preference (the shipped `$:/config/lares/ProjectionFilter` withholds TW5's status prefix and the story and history lists), and the shore log page (`$:/lares/shore/log`: the vessel's log records, one per distinct event, by counts per kind, then a kind, then raw, with ack, fold to the month's ash, and open) re-pack the house skin. The next labelled GENESIS RE-BAKE carries these bytes and deletes this row; a standing house folds once it adopts that house skin, and until then lares spirit om and hum read unfolded and name the read that shows the absent fold; the floor gate (the floor-queue module, its filter and page, the budget view ordered by verdict); the security-class filter (lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/filters/security-class: the familiar's cold-read list matched over a diff's paths); the home preference (the boot pointer and the open-wiki reactor burn; a lit face reads `$:/config/lares/home/wiki` at light).

The projection preference: the grammar-cache module carries the shipped `$:/config/lares/ProjectionFilter` base text, which now withholds TW5's status prefix and the story and history lists (UI navigation state, as TW5's own SaverFilter keeps them unsaved). The next labelled GENESIS RE-BAKE carries these bytes and deletes this row; until then a founded vessel's in-VM wiki reads the earlier base, and the daemon-side projector reads the new one from dist. The home preference re-packs the grammar skin too (the active-wiki meme burns its boot pointer).
